title: Why Symmetry Needs Algebra
question: Why does one idea, the group, appear in crystals, codes and equations?
hook: The same small set of rules describes shuffled cards, turned crystals and unsolvable equations.
idea: A group captures symmetry by abstracting what it takes to combine and undo transformations, which is why it appears across mathematics and physics.

beats.prompt: Sort each description into the kind of group it belongs to.
items: Bijections of a set, closed under composition and inverses
Invertible matrices over a field, closed under products and inverses
Acts on a vector space by linear transformations
beats.explain: Both are transformation groups; the permutation kind acts on a set and the matrix kind acts on a vector space.

beats.prompt: Put these moments in the history of group theory in order.
items: Galois uses groups to study solvability of equations (1830s)
The theory of groups is unified (starting around 1880)
Lie starts using groups for analytic problems (1884)
The classification of finite simple groups is published (mostly 1960 to 2004)
beats.explain: Groups grew from equation solving, through unification and geometry, to a huge 20th century classification.

beats.prompt: Take all possible shuffles of a set, then keep only some of them, as long as the kept ones stay closed under composition and inverses. What do you have?

choices.label: A permutation group sitting inside the full symmetric group
A new object unrelated to the symmetric group
choices.feedback: It seems new, but any permutation group is a subgroup of the symmetric group of its set.

choices.label: Always the whole symmetric group again
choices.feedback: Closure alone does not force every shuffle to be kept; smaller collections qualify.

beats.explain: Any permutation group is a subgroup of the symmetric group of its set.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Any permutation group is a subgroup of the symmetric group on its set.
For n at least 5, the alternating group on n elements is simple.
Simple means it has no proper normal subgroups.
So this fact shows general equations of degree three and four cannot be solved in radicals.
beats.explain: The simplicity fact plays a key role in the impossibility for degree five and higher, not degrees three and four.
